page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the c2d family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, utilizing the x86_64 architecture with simultaneous multithreading enabled at 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 32 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The AMD EPYC 7B13 processor delivers strong single-core performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 2922.28, placing it in the top 25% of tested instances. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% with a stress-ng multi-core score of 5861.67 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3741.0. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is average, measuring 46.82 GB/sec for read operations and 27.55 GB/sec for write operations, while small cached block read bandwidth is weak at 275.84 GB/sec.

The instance exhibits weak performance in parallelized workloads, such as software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and database operations. Static web serving throughput is also low at 5.54 GB/sec. However, single-threaded operations like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels. This profile suggests the instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling, such as caching layers, lightweight in-memory databases, or single-threaded data processing tasks.

It offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance in the top 25%. Conversely, multi-core performance is weak, as shown by lower scores in multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and database operations. Memory bandwidth for large blocks remains average, with read speeds of 46.82 GB/sec. This hardware profile is suited for memory-intensive, single-threaded applications, caching systems, and lightweight database workloads that benefit from dedicated memory capacity rather than dense multi-core processing power.
